html:
Empowering Families and Educators to Keep Children Safe

Date: September 7–13, 2025
Theme: “Every Conversation Matters: Shifting Conversation to Action”

Each year, National Child Protection Week—led by NAPCAN—calls on Australians to unite in protecting children from abuse and neglect. The 2025 theme is a powerful reminder that safeguarding children begins with open, honest conversations—and ends with meaningful action.

👶 Why Early Education Is Central to Child Protection

Early childhood educators are often the first trusted adults outside the family to observe a child’s wellbeing. In these formative years, children build relationships, express emotions, and begin to understand boundaries. That’s why early education services are uniquely positioned to:

  • Recognize signs of distress or abuse
  • Create safe, nurturing environments
  • Support families with guidance and referrals
  • Model respectful, protective behavior

Child protection isn’t just a policy—it’s a daily practice embedded in every interaction, routine, and learning moment.

🏛️ What’s New in Victoria: Department of Education Reforms

In response to growing concerns around child safety, the Victorian Department of Education has introduced significant reforms in 2025 to strengthen protections across early childhood services:

  • Mandatory child safety training for all staff and volunteers
  • Stricter device usage policies to prevent inappropriate content exposure
  • Enhanced Working With Children Check (WWCC) procedures
  • Unannounced compliance visits to ensure standards are upheld
  • New national register to track educator conduct and safety breaches

These changes reflect a broader commitment to making child safety non-negotiable in every learning space.

👨👩👧 Resources for Parents: How You Can Help

Protecting children starts at home. Here are trusted resources to help you talk to your child and take action:

  • 🧠 eSafety for Parents: Tips on digital safety, screen time, and online risks
  • 📘 NAPCAN’s Parent Resources: Guides on protective behaviors, conversations, and community support
  • 🏫 Child Safe Standards – Victoria: Understand your rights and responsibilities
  • 📞 Child Protection Helpline (Victoria): 1300 360 391 – for urgent concerns or advice

💬 Final Thought

Whether you're a parent, educator, or community member, your voice matters. This week is a chance to reflect, learn, and recommit to the safety of every child. Because when we protect children, we build stronger families—and a better future.

title: Child Safe Code of Conduct – quick guide
excerpt: A full version of our Child Safe Code of Conduct is available in KinderM8. All staff, students and volunteers must read and follow our full Child Safe Code of Conduct DO: · Always put children’s...
html:
A full version of our Child Safe Code of Conduct is available in KinderM8. All staff, students and volunteers must read and follow our full Child Safe Code of Conduct

DO:

· Always put children’s safety, health and wellbeing first

· Follow our child safety policies and legal obligations, including for mandatory reporting

· Respond immediately to any concern, risk, disclosure or incident

· Use positive, respectful and non-intrusive behaviour guidance

· Maintain professional boundaries and conduct with children and families

· Use physical contact only when appropriate (e.g., to comfort, prevent harm, assist with care)

· Ensure supervision is active, constant and appropriate for each child

· Communicate respectfully and professionally, including online

· Follow our rules for digital devices, photography, technology, and record keeping

· Welcome and support all children and families, regardless of background, identity or ability

DO NOT:

· Engage in any behaviour that harms, risks harm, or exploits a child

· Use physical punishment, shaming, intimidation or humiliation

· Show favouritism, develop inappropriate relationships, or ignore boundary violations

· Communicate privately or online with children

· Have your personal digital devices in your possession while you are with children

· Take or share images or recordings of children without written parental consent

· Make negative, discriminatory or inappropriate comments about a child or their family

· Be alone with a child or work in ways that are not visible to others

· Talk about adult topics or use adult language around children

· Smoke, vape, or be under the influence of drugs or alcohol at work

**Breaches and suspected breaches must be reported to the nominated supervisor and/or approved provider either in person, by telephone on 9000 8916 or via email makayla.menzies@edu-play.com.au

If the breach relates to harm or the risk of harm to a child, staff must follow our Child Protection Policy and Procedures**

title: Am I eligible for FREE 3-4 year old kinder?

html:
Investing in Their Future: Understanding Free Kindergarten within Long Daycare

Providing your child with a strong educational foundation is a priority for every parent. An exciting opportunity exists for families with 3 and 4-year-old children: access to free kindergarten programs delivered within long daycare settings. This initiative aims to make quality early learning more accessible and integrated into families' existing childcare arrangements.

What is Free Kindergarten in Long Daycare?

Eligible long daycare providers can offer a kindergarten program, delivered by a qualified early childhood teacher, for a set number of hours per week to families. This means your child can benefit from a structured, play-based learning experience within their familiar long-daycare environment, without incurring additional kindergarten fees.

Key Benefits of Free Kindergarten in Long Daycare:

  • Convenience and Continuity of Care: Integrating kindergarten within your existing long daycare service offers seamless transitions and consistent care for your child throughout the day.
  • Qualified Early Childhood Educators: The kindergarten program is led by qualified teachers who are experts in early childhood development and deliver a curriculum focused on fostering essential skills.
  • Developmentally Appropriate Learning: The curriculum emphasizes play-based learning, encouraging children's social, emotional, cognitive, language, and physical development in a stimulating and engaging way.
  • Preparation for School: The program helps children build foundational literacy and numeracy skills, develop independence, and learn how to interact effectively in a group setting, easing their transition to primary school.
  • Financial Relief: Eliminating or reducing kindergarten fees can significantly reduce the overall cost of early childhood education for eligible families.

Understanding Eligibility:

Eligibility for free kindergarten within long daycare generally depends on the following criteria:

  • Age of the Child: The child must be aged three or four years old by a specific date. Specific age cut-offs may vary slightly depending on state or territory regulations.
  • Enrolment in an Approved Long Daycare Service: The long daycare service your child attends must be an approved provider participating in the free kindergarten initiative.
  • Number of Funded Hours: There is typically a cap on the number of free kindergarten hours a child can access per week (e.g., 15 hours per school term). Families may still utilize additional paid hours of care within the long daycare setting.
  • Residency Requirements: Usually, the child must be a resident of the relevant state or territory.

Taking the Next Steps:

To conclude the next steps and reach out for more info, contact Makayla, the centre director, on the "contact us" page or by using the email makayla@altonaearlyeducation.com.au

Investing in your child's early years is crucial. Free kindergarten within long daycare offers a valuable opportunity to provide them with high-quality learning experiences in a convenient and supportive environment. Take the initiative to explore your eligibility and unlock this potential for your child's future success.

title: Ditch the Time-Outs: Embrace "Time-In" for Better Behavior
excerpt: The Community Child Care Association dives into the controversial world of time-outs and why they might not be the best option for managing children's behaviour. The Australian Children’s Education &...
html:
The Community Child Care Association dives into the controversial world of time-outs and why they might not be the best option for managing children's behaviour.
The Australian Children’s Education & Care Quality Authority (ACECQA) states that time-outs are a no-go. Instead, they champion the "time-in" approach.

What's that, you ask? It's all about quality one-on-one time between educators and children to help them calm down and understand their emotions. This method emphasizes building strong relationships and meeting the child's needs—no lectures needed.

Celebrating Special Persons Day At Edu-Play Early Learning

At Edu-Play Early Learning, we believe that every child is a unique individual, and their learning journey is beautifully enriched by the special people in their lives. That's why Special Persons Day holds a cherished place in our hearts. This year, we opened our doors to parents, grandparents, uncles, aunts, and special friends for a delightful afternoon tea, filled with warmth, laughter, and a showcase of our children's learning experiences.

A Heartfelt Welcome

Families began to arrive at our vibrant learning center, excited to share in the magic of the day. The smiles on the children’s faces illuminated the room, each one bustling with enthusiasm to introduce their special guests to their friends and the work they had accomplished throughout the year.

Showcasing Learning In Action

After the delicious tea, the children excitedly showcased their various learning activities. Whether it was art projects, science experiments, or literacy displays, each presentation highlighted their unique talents and the skills they have developed over the year. This was a wonderful opportunity for the children to shine, demonstrating their knowledge and confidence while engaging their special guests in conversations about their studies.

Many parents and grandparents beamed with pride as they watched their little ones articulate what they had learned, from counting and colors to sharing stories about their favorite books. It was truly a joy to see the bonds strengthen between children and their special persons as they celebrated their achievements together.

Looking Forward

As we reflect on the memories created during Special Persons Day, we’re filled with gratitude for the supportive families and friends who enrich our community. We look forward to many more events that allow us to celebrate our children’s growth and the special people who inspire them every day.

At Edu-Play Early Learning, we understand that education is a partnership, and we are committed to nurturing every child's potential with the support of their special persons. Thank you to everyone who made this day a resounding success – your love and involvement make all the difference in our children’s educational journeys. We can’t wait for next year’s celebrations!

Until next time, keep celebrating the special bonds that make learning so much more meaningful!

title: Montessori or Reggio: Which Approach To Kindergarten?
excerpt: There are numerous early childhood philosophies that guide educators and parents in fostering the growth and development of young children. While these philosophies can be effective for many...
html:
There are numerous early childhood philosophies that guide educators and parents in fostering the growth and development of young children. While these philosophies can be effective for many children, it is important to recognize that they may not suit every child.

One such philosophy is the Montessori method, which emphasizes independence, freedom within limits, and respect for a child's natural development. While this approach works well for children who thrive in structured environments and are self-motivated, other children may struggle with the amount of freedom and responsibility given to them.

For children who need more structure and guidance, a different philosophy such as Reggio Emilia or Waldorf education may be more suited to their needs. These philosophies focus on creativity, social interaction, and hands-on learning, providing a more nurturing and supportive environment for children who may struggle with independence.

Ultimately, it is important to recognize that each child is unique and may require a different approach in their early childhood education. By understanding and adapting to the individual needs of each child, we can ensure that they receive the support and guidance they need to thrive.

At Edu-Play Early Learning, we know that most children learn best when incorporating elements from each philosophy that best suit your child. Our small daycare kindergarten allows us the time and resources to create an individualised learning method for your child. This is part of our unique approach to early learning.

title: Unlocking Potential: Play-Based Learning Is The Key to Early Childhood Success
excerpt: In Altona, Edu-Play Early Learning is reshaping early childhood education with its innovative play-based approach tailored for preschoolers. This forward-thinking kindergarten prioritizes engaging...
html:
In Altona, Edu-Play Early Learning is reshaping early childhood education with its innovative play-based approach tailored for preschoolers. This forward-thinking kindergarten prioritizes engaging activities that stimulate creativity, problem-solving, and a lifelong love for learning.

Founder Grace Azzopardi articulates the mission: "We aim to unlock every child's potential by fostering curiosity and creativity through play-based learning." This philosophy is supported by the research of Dr. Kathy Hirsh-Pasek, a leading expert in developmental psychology, and her colleague Dr. Roberta Michnick Golinkoff. Their studies, such as "Becoming Brilliant," highlight the cognitive and social benefits of playful learning experiences over rote methods, emphasizing play's role in nurturing creativity and problem-solving.

The American Academy of Pediatrics also supports this, highlighting play's significance in children's overall well-being.

Edu-Play's curriculum is designed to captivate young minds, offering activities from block-building for math concepts to storytelling for language skills. Many families attest to the transformative impact of this approach on literacy, numeracy, and cognitive development.

In conclusion, Edu-Play Early Learning champions play-based learning as a superior alternative to traditional rote methods, preparing children to thrive in the 21st century as confident, creative learners.

title: Supporting Early Childhood Australia's Statement On Play
excerpt: What is ECA's statement on play? ECA's statement on play is a comprehensive document that outlines the importance of play in early childhood education. It highlights the many benefits of play,...
html:
What is ECA's statement on play?

ECA's statement on play is a comprehensive document that outlines the importance of play in early childhood education. It highlights the many benefits of play, including cognitive, social, emotional, and physical development. The statement also emphasizes the role of educators in creating play-based learning environments that foster creativity, curiosity, and problem-solving skills.

How does ECA's statement support our play focus?

By aligning with ECA's statement on play, we ensure that our approach to early childhood education is evidence-based and grounded in best practices. We believe that children learn best through play, and ECA's statement reinforces this belief. It provides us with a framework to guide our curriculum and pedagogy, ensuring that play is at the center of everything we do.

Furthermore, ECA's statement on play helps us advocate for the importance of play in early childhood education. It provides us with a strong foundation to engage with parents, policymakers, and the wider community, and to raise awareness about the value of play in children's lives. By sharing ECA's statement, we can inspire others to prioritize play and create play-rich environments for children.

Why is play so important?

Play is not just a way for children to have fun; it is a vital component of their overall development. Through play, children learn important skills such as problem-solving, communication, and collaboration. Play also helps children develop their imagination, creativity, and self-expression.

Additionally, play allows children to explore their world, make sense of their experiences, and develop a sense of agency and autonomy. It promotes physical activity and helps children develop their gross and fine motor skills. Play also supports children's social and emotional development, as they learn to navigate relationships, regulate their emotions, and develop empathy and resilience.

How can parents and educators support play?

Parents and educators play a crucial role in supporting play. They can create an environment that encourages and values play, providing children with open-ended materials, time, and space to explore and engage in imaginative play. They can also be active participants in play, joining in and extending children's play experiences.

Furthermore, parents and educators can advocate for play in their communities and schools, raising awareness about its importance and advocating for policies that prioritize play-based learning. By working together, we can ensure that play remains a fundamental part of every child's early years.

At ECA, we are committed to promoting and supporting play in early childhood education. By aligning with ECA's statement on play, we are able to provide children with the best possible learning experiences, fostering their holistic development and setting them up for a lifetime of learning and success.

title: Tiny Kindergartens, Big Bonds: Small Kindergartens Foster Secure Attachment
excerpt: Forget sterile classrooms and endless rows of tiny chairs. Imagine a kindergarten where warmth trumps worksheets, and tiny humans find not just knowledge, but a safe haven. This is the magic of small...
html:
Forget sterile classrooms and endless rows of tiny chairs. Imagine a kindergarten where warmth trumps worksheets, and tiny humans find not just knowledge, but a safe haven. This is the magic of small kindergartens, where secure attachment isn't just a theory, it's a daily cuddle puddle.

But what exactly is this "secure attachment" everyone's whispering about? It's like a secret superpower, a deep-down confidence that your grown-up is your anchor, your superhero cape, your personal ray of sunshine (minus the tantrums, hopefully). It's knowing, without a doubt, that you'll be heard, held, and helped, no matter what mini-meltdown you have over misplaced Legos.

So, how do these tiny kindergartens become attachment-building champions? It's all about quality, not quantity. With fewer kids to juggle, teachers can weave themselves into the very fabric of each little life. They become not just educators, but cuddlers, boo-boo bandaiders, and cheerleaders for even the most wobbly tower of blocks.

Imagine a kindergarten teacher who spots a quiet sniffle before it turns into a tsunami of tears, or one who scoops up a frustrated builder with a gentle "Let's try a different way, champ!" This kind of personalized attention is like emotional fertilizer, nurturing the tiny roots of trust and security.

And because there are fewer tiny voices demanding attention, these teachers have the superpower of time. Time to listen, to play, to follow a curious butterfly all the way to the playground. This unhurried presence sends a powerful message: "You matter, exactly as you are."

The result? Children who blossom like sunflowers in a greenhouse of love. They become better problem-solvers, knowing they have a safety net for daring experiments. They're more emotionally intelligent, able to navigate their own feelings and empathize with others. And they forge deeper friendships, built on the bedrock of trust they learned in their tiny, but mighty, kindergarten.

So, the next time you see a small kindergarten, don't just see a school. See a launchpad for little astronauts, a jungle gym for emotions, and a haven where secure attachment isn't just a buzzword, it's the building block of bright futures.

For more information, following the link below:
